findings: Original ParseLobbyBackendDoc converts JSON override values to strings and attempts RegisterDvarByString for each; a failed individual registration does not change the document parse-success flag.
A missing dvar lookup takes the RegisterDvarByString branch at0x14107D4D2, creates a permanent STRING dvar with flags0x100, then returns its pointer.
ApplyDvarOverrides consumes264-byte entries and SetDvarByString handles type9 via the string setter; existing BOOL0 and numeric types use their native typed setters.
The new numeric0/1 acknowledgement values are therefore accepted as strings by older clients without those registrations. No document-wide unknown-name rejection occurs in this native path.
The backend native envelope retains the128 override bound.
